staged_batch_size_rules: Use the current deployment's modeling_batch_max_items bound before submission (default 100; Host supplies the current value when unavailable to the role).

Split a larger staged projection in dependency order without changing candidate meaning. Each part has a distinct plan/client batch ID and keys, exact review and its own dry_run/apply_atomic; cross-part references use earlier actual receipts, and depends_on is local to one Batch.
A definite batch_limit_exceeded rejection before any write permits fresh part plans. Preserve the rejected plan, do not raise the platform limit, and never replay already applied parts.
purpose: Protocol-only, platform-generic construction contract for immutable Modeling Batches. This reference contains no domain model, scenario target, or acceptance answer.
create_identity_rules: For create commands, a nonempty explicit resource-specific ID field (such as class_id, property_id, relation_type_id or entity_id) is accepted and preserved in resource_outputs.resource_id. If omitted or empty, the platform generates the deterministic UUID5 output from batch_id, ontology_id, client_item_id and command_kind.

prepare normalizes the resource-specific payload ID to that selected output; it does not replace a supplied nonempty ID with a different deterministic ID. resource_id is a receipt output key, not a generic create payload field; use only the ID field allowed by that command's payload contract.

A candidate_item_id is a neutral semantic identity. Protocol preserves candidate correspondence through the approved decision_bindings and identity_bindings; it need not equal the platform resource ID or every create payload ID.

An explicit ID does not authorize Modeling or Protocol to guess its platform IRI. For preprotection or a same-batch confirmed L3 node plus enum mapping, Host may provide an authoritative intended identity by calling the actual backend ModelingCommandHandlerRegistry.outputs_for with the deployed Settings, the planned command context and a nonempty explicit resource-specific payload ID. With that explicit ID the output IRI depends on the actual namespace/resource kind/ID, not the UUID5 fallback or a not-yet-created internal Batch ID; do not use this route for omitted IDs. This is a planned identity, not an existing resource or proof of application.

Use that Host-provided intended resource_iri only for preprotection membership and the approved same-batch L3 attachment/enum semantic_value. The create identity binding remains a future receipt_ref with resource_iri/evidence_ref null. Modeling does not author platform identities, and dependent later stages still bind real receipt/read outputs.

Keep the explicit ID and approved plan unchanged, compare actual dry_run/apply resource_outputs against the intended resource_id/resource_iri, and stop the affected write/dependencies on drift. Existing confirmation, unlock, content-bound/translation approval, protection and application gates remain mandatory; do not silently replace the intended IRI.

rules: column matches identifier_pattern; property_iri when supplied is an absolute RDF IRI, required for business_key. Unknown fields are rejected.
Each step has exactly one listed field set. Table names and columns match identifier_pattern. Mapping references are absolute IRIs; roles are nonempty strings.

from_columns/to_columns are nonempty equal-length arrays. All steps use the same form. Adjacent table steps match to_table/from_table; mapping steps match to_mapping_iri/from_mapping_iri and to_role/from_role.
Exactly these fields: field is an absolute property IRI; operator and value are nonempty strings. No operator enum is imposed by the compiler.

source_key and optional schema_version/row_grain/row_scope are nonempty strings or null. record_key_columns/object_key_columns are string arrays (possibly empty) or null. identifiers/field_meanings are arrays (possibly empty) or null.
identifier_rules: columns is a nonempty array of nonempty strings; property_iri optional absolute IRI/null; scope/correspondence optional nonempty string/null.
field_meaning_rules: column matches identifier_pattern; conversion_rule_iri is optional absolute IRI/null; other fields optional nonempty string/null.

rules: step_semantics is an array (possibly empty) or null; each step_index is a unique nonnegative integer, never a boolean. join_type/cardinality may be absent/null.
relationship_meaning/duplicate_risk/execution_prerequisite/additional_condition are optional nonempty strings/null; condition_rule_iri is optional absolute IRI/null.
Optional absolute IRI or null.

contexts is an array (possibly empty) or null; context_key is a unique nonempty string. applicability/base_role/duplicate_handling are optional nonempty strings/null; base_mapping_iri optional absolute IRI/null.
join_mapping_iris/conversion_rule_iris are arrays of absolute IRIs (possibly empty) when present, not null. property_bindings/counted_identity are arrays (possibly empty) or null.

Each property_bindings item has exactly all property_binding_fields: absolute property/table-mapping IRIs, role nonempty string/null, column identifier. Each counted_identity item has exactly all counted_identity_fields: absolute table-mapping IRI, role nonempty string/null, nonempty string array columns.

Every mapping_definition object and nested member is closed to its listed fields; optional fields may be absent. mapping_definition itself may be absent/null. Empty objects are accepted except table_mapping, which requires the source_key key.
Only canonical *_iri names carry platform references. Preserve unknowns, scope, conversion meaning and approved business semantics; never choose them from a field name.

Mapping candidates remain unchanged. Protocol recursively resolves {definition_ref:item_id} or governed existing-resource wrappers to actual authorized read/formal receipt identities before submitting the corresponding canonical carrier; unresolved references remain repairable and mapping writes stay closed. The same-batch confirmed L3 semantic_value may instead use the Host-authoritative intended identity under create_identity_rules; this is not a guessed future IRI or automatic alias passthrough.

Semantic neutral aliases are not Batch payload fields: mapped_class/mapped_class_ref -> mapped_class_iri; mapped_definition/mapped_definition_ref -> mapped_definition_iri; property_ref -> property_iri; table_mapping_ref -> table_mapping_iri; semantic_value_ref -> semantic_value; relation_type/relation_type_ref -> relation_type_iri; time_field_ref -> time_field; measure_property_ref -> measure_property_iri. Aliases and canonical values must agree if both were authored; never silently override a conflict.

For mapping-form join steps, canonical fields are from_mapping_iri/to_mapping_iri and from_role/to_role. source_table_ref/target_table_ref are not accepted canonical fields or automatic aliases; use the candidate's explicitly approved endpoint meanings to bind them to the matching mapping-role pair, or ask for repair if that meaning is unresolved.

Nested references likewise use canonical property_iri/conversion_rule_iri/condition_rule_iri/base_mapping_iri/join_mapping_iris/table_mapping_iri/conversion_rule_iris fields as listed above; resolve wrappers recursively through arrays and objects, including metric contexts. Column/table names and schema_source stay authorized physical metadata, not resource references.

These carriers do not waive schema/data-mapping scope, value confirmation, candidate/translation approval, protection, dry-run/apply or receipt/readback requirements. Independently approved ordinary stages may proceed while unresolved mapping stages stay closed.
mapping_reference_binding.example_note: Examples use syntax placeholders only. Their IRIs denote stand-ins for real authorized receipt/read outputs, not namespace guesses or permitted current-run identities.

session_id.description: MCP tool argument; identifies the Build Session.

expected_workspace_version.invariant: Required in every mode and must equal the current workspace version at Service submission.

depends_on.invariant: Every entry must name a client_item_id in THIS SAME batch: the platform resolves dependencies against the current batch's items only, so naming an item from an earlier batch yields a blocking invalid_dependency finding. Cross-batch ordering is guaranteed by submitting batches sequentially in dependency order and is never expressed in the payload

competency_question_ids.invariant: Keep empty (the default) unless the platform project actually contains those CompetencyQuestion rows: R3.0-011 question pools are run artifacts only and are never registered as platform resources, so syncing pool IDs here yields blocking competency_question_not_found findings and the batch fails closed

class_iris.description: Full formal Class set (R3.0-009 §4.1/§6.2). Entries are class ids or absolute IRIs, deduplicated by the compiler. Omitted, null and [] are the same legal zero-member state; no placeholder Class is invented.

create_operation.invariant: Operation v1 validation remains unchanged; active Operations require a nonempty tool binding. No secrets or Action annotations. Association nodes link to this resource, never merge identities.

cross_batch_application_contract.purpose: Platform-generic, create-only topological schedule for applying one immutable semantic candidate across Modeling Batches. It adds no business semantics and does not change candidate meaning.
cross_batch_application_contract.ordered_schedule: class -> property/relation type -> entity -> receipt/read bind generated IDs/IRIs -> relation

formal_binding.workspace_version: For every next Batch, use the current workspace version only from the immediately prior formal apply receipt or required platform read.
formal_binding.generated_identifiers: Before the relation stage, bind generated resource IDs and absolute resource IRIs only from formal create receipts or required platform reads; never guess, synthesize, or forward-reference them.

cross_batch_application_contract.candidate_invariant: Protocol treats the Modeling candidate and its dependencies as immutable semantic input. It may schedule platform application across Batches, but must not mutate candidate meaning or reorder candidate semantics.
forbidden: delegate exact Batch Items to Modeling
cross_batch_application_contract.binding_conflict: If a required dependency cannot be bound from a formal receipt or platform read, return a concrete translation conflict before the dangerous write.

semantic_retrieval_completion_contract.purpose: Platform-generic completion rules for ontology-scoped retrieval. It contains no business semantics or source-tracing payload.

ordinary_v3_execution.scope: Resolve the run-owned project and ontology from receipts or reads; query_semantic_context uses project_id, scope_mode=ontologies, and exact ontology_ids.
ordinary_v3_execution.question_partition: Issue one narrow query per competency question and keep resource_types narrow when the needed kind is known.
ordinary_v3_execution.recall: A degraded or unavailable vector index is incomplete; retry the same question with lexical search.
ordinary_v3_execution.pagination: Consume context_cursor before next_match_cursor. Never send both cursors or reuse a context cursor across match pages.
ordinary_v3_execution.completion: A receipt requires scope-correct, value-correct, non-truncated results and successful continuation whenever paging is required.

successful_receipt_requires: successful continuation whenever paging is required
incomplete_conditions: receipt/read count, identity, workspace, delta, or ownership drift

fallback.allowed: An incomplete or degraded generic query may use the ordinary scoped readback path before returning a typed retrieval conflict.
fallback.readback: Bind final graph, workspace and source signature, compare applied deltas with entity and statement reads, and preserve exact predicate/value and scope checks.
fallback.cursor: The stable unfiltered Session Batch inventory must have no next_cursor; statement and entity reads remain bounded and explicit.

property_read_contract.availability: MCP tools below are usable only when advertised in the current role catalog. If absent, request the authorized Host's original scoped HTTP read envelope through the existing Owner channel; do not call an unadvertised tool or widen permissions.

http.identity_filter_note: HTTP uses entity for the receipt/read-bound property IRI; MCP uses entity_iri.

rules: Bind ontology_id to the existing authorized workspace/receipt; items[].iri is the returned property identity. Preserve paging/truncation limits. get_ontology_read_model does not accept property-list.

http.body: Use the same project_id, scope_mode, ontology_ids, query and optional timeout_seconds/result_limit fields.

rules: Use only the authorized project_id and ontology_ids; replace the synthetic example IRI with an existing receipt/read-bound property IRI. This read-only scoped query retrieves the property's current predicates/values without guessing its identity; respect the returned scope, including any inferred graphs.
A concept/fact no_match or unsupported_read_model response does not establish property absence; use the advertised authorized read tool and preserve unresolved read limits.

update_property.identity: At least one of property_id or property_iri is required, using the existing authorized identity binding; update preserves that property identity. ontology_id belongs to the Batch envelope, not this payload.

description.server_behavior: Omitted or null leaves the comment unchanged; an empty string clears it; a nonempty string replaces it.

semantic_definition.description: Existing R4.0-002 common declaration; retain the candidate's unchanged declaration when supplying an approved correction.

rules: Supply only approved changed fields and any required unchanged semantic declaration; omitted/null name, description, datatype and object_class_id do not update those fields. A description-only correction does not recreate the property or change its domain/type/range.

When the approved plan's existing identity binding carries a resource_iri, send property_iri with that exact value, not a short property_id; property_id remains valid where the authorized target contract is ID-based and the ID matches.

update_entity.identity: entity_id or entity_iri, using the existing authorized identity binding.
update_entity.annotation_update: Annotations replace as objects, clear with null, and remain unchanged when omitted.

ordered_schedule: class -> property/relation type -> entity -> receipt/read bind generated IDs/IRIs -> relation
